Once upon a time, a cat named Sunny sat on the grass. The sun was hot and Sunny was thirsty. He saw a lemonade stand near the window. But nobody could read the sign. Sunny could read it. "I can help," said Sunny.
Sunny found some big paper. He held it up. The words were small. He had to make them big so everyone could see.
A friendly printer lived under the table. It hummed softly. "What do you need?" asked the printer.
"I need you to print a sign for my lemonade stand," said Sunny.
The printer rolled its white paper into itself. Then it pressed down and pushed out fresh words. A purple sign appeared on the paper. "Look!" said Sunny. "The words are big. Everyone can see."
The man at the stand read the sign. "Yummy lemonade!" he said. People bought cups of lemonade. Sunny drank one and smiled. He sat on the bench and purred. The cat helped, and that made him happy.

A paper got stuck inside Leo. It caught the paper path. The printer made a beeping sound. The paper was bumpy with jammed pieces. Finn reached into the printer opening. Finn pulled out a little teddy bear that had gotten stuck. It was not a real bear but paper stuck together. Finn freed the paper. Then the family printed their photos. The photos came out perfectly smooth. Everyone laughed and hugged Leo. The end.

Luna woke up suddenly! "Ouch!" said Luna. She jumped off the printer. The bird sang a song. Luna walked away slowly. The bird flew out the window. It was a funny thing to happen.

"The tray is empty," Tom said sadly. He needed paper to print. Without paper, the printer cannot do its job. Tom looked around the room. He found a roll of paper near the shelf. He put it in the tray. Now the printer started to work. Warm paper came out, and a nice card was ready. Tom gave the card to his mom. She hugged Tom and said, "Thank you, honey." Tom learned that even when doing something seems hard at first, if you look for the right tools, everything works out fine.

The lesson is: carry things forward and keep the world clean.

Then he sat down and felt gray and tired. He did not want to play anymore. A bird flew near. "Are you okay?" the bird asked. "I am sad because I keep pressing the machine," Milo said. The bird landed on the table. "Maybe the machine needs rest," the bird said gently. Milo thought about it. He stepped back. He looked at the quiet printer. He did not press it again. He took a breath and felt a little better. Sometimes you have to wait and be gentle.

Then they took a new piece of paper. They put it where the old paper was. The machine printed the card. The card was perfect. The family was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a red table in the kitchen. The sun was up and bright. A table is where things sit. On the table sat a big tray with one last sheet of paper inside. The paper was warm from the sun. It felt soft and light.
A little bird came and sat on top of the tray. "I want a cracker," said the bird. "I will eat the last sheet of paper."
The bird picked at the paper. It tore right down the middle. One half stayed on the tray. The other half went to the floor.
"Oh no," said the bird. "The paper is torn!"
The bird fluttered away. The little piece on the floor made a sound like a crinkly leaf. The tray had only half a sheet now.
"That is not enough paper," said a small bug who heard the story. "We need all of it for the letters."
So the bird flew back. She used her beak to pick up the torn edge. Then she tore that piece into tiny bits and ate them one by one. The tray was full again.

The calculator was friendly. The calculator said, "I can help." Finn gave the calculator a look. The calculator opened its case. Inside, it found a small screw. The calculator turned the screw. The screw fit into the printer. The printer hummed. Papers came out again. Finn was happy. Finn said, "Thank you, calculator." The calculator said, "We work well together." Finn smiled and used the printer again.

Her sister smiled and said, "That is okay. We can add more ink together." So Mia put ink on the page and printed it again. This time the card had sweet drawings of a sun, a cake, and flowers. Mia tore the card and gave it to her sister. Her sister clapped her hands. It was a good day.

Max felt sad. He looked around and saw a blue rug on the floor. He sat on the rug and cried softly. His mother came and asked what was wrong. Max said, "The printer broke and I cannot print the invitations." His mother laughed gently and said, "I will help you fix it." Together they put the printer back together. Soon the printer worked again. Max printed all the invitations. When the friends came, they clapped their hands. Everyone had a wonderful party.

A paper airplane can fly very far if you fold it well. That is a small lesson for every child.

One day Kate felt something warm and soft on her back. It was a piece of paper with ink on it. She was so fluffy and soft. She ran to her hole in the wall. "I will keep this paper," she said. From then on every night she would print one sheet for her sleeping space.

The duck gave him an orange. From now on the duck used real batter, not the printer.

The frog could print a picture in a book. The frog went to the dark room and sat by Pip. "I am scared," said the frog. "Come sit next to me," said Pip. Then Pip turned on. Pip hummed and beeped and took a piece of paper. Pip printed the picture of the frog. Now the room was not so dark anymore. The frog was happy. Pip learned that even small things can help a friend feel safe. It was a nice lesson for everyone.

After the picture was done, the drop slid down onto the page. It saw green trees and brown mountains. It saw a yellow sun. Then a person took the page outside. The drop dried up but it remembered all the colors. It felt full and happy.

She found another way to draw the car. She used crayons. The picture was not perfect but it was good. Zoe learned that you have to be patient when things go wrong. You can still make something nice.

He was glad the rain passed. Now he could jump across the lily pads again.

The printer turned on. But rain came outside. Raindrops hit the window. Water dripped onto the paper. The printer tried to print. The ink ran in raindrops. The sunny picture became a mess. "No no no," said the children. They looked out the window. Sun was shining again. The clouds moved away. "Wait," said the mom. She held up a clean sheet of paper. "Try again," she said. The children helped. The printer made a bright yellow sun. Yellow and white circles went on the paper. It was neat and perfect. The children put the book back on the shelf. The book now had a sunny picture inside. Every time they opened it, they smiled.

He printed a small bird instead. The bird flew across the paper. It was cute and bright. Max was happy. "See?" said the printer. "Small things fit me well." Max smiled. He put the bird picture on the wall. Next to it he printed a small sun. The sun went behind the bird. It looked like the bird flew into the sun. Max was glad. The big sky picture waited for another day. Maybe later. For now, the small prints were perfect.

Instead of the calculator, it printed a picture of a farmer holding a big hat. Instead of the farm, it printed a mountain far away. Ted looked at the prints and felt very lonely. The calculator was missing from the picture. The farm was missing from the picture. Ted said, "That is not right." He pulled the paper out and tried again. This time he moved the calculator closer to the paper edge. The printer still did not print the calculator right. Ted had an idea. He held the calculator flat on top of the paper. The printer printed both the farmer and the calculator on the same page. Ted laughed and hugged the prints. The picture was correct at last.

The crayon was bright and red. He pushed the button. The printer printed a picture of a red dog. Buster wagged his tail. "This is great," said Leo. Mom and Dad clapped their hands. The new printer made a happy humming sound. It printed many more pictures. Everyone was so happy. The end.

Once upon a time, it was a rainy day. Tess sat by the window. Raindrops tapped on the glass. She fed a page into the printer. "Please print this song for me," said Tess. The printer started to work. But the paper got wet. Water dripped onto the paper. The ink ran away. The words became smudged and blurry. "Oh no," said Tess. The song looked lonely and sad. She looked out the window. The rain did not stop. She waited. Then she heard a soft splash outside. A frog jumped onto the step. "Can I help?" said the frog. Tess handed the wet paper to the frog. The frog lifted his foot. A clean spot appeared on the paper. The ink stayed clean there. "Thank you," said Tess. The frog hopped away. Tess read the song again. She laughed. The end.

It printed all the pages right. Milo smiled. Pip the mouse peeked out. "Good idea," said Pip. Everything was neat again. The end.

But the printer stayed on. The printer hummed and printed quietly. Lily felt better. She knew the printer would always stay on. Later that day, a balloon floated up into the office. The balloon bumped into Lily. Lily floated up too. She floated around the dark room. The printer kept printing. Lily kept glowing. The printer lit the whole room. Everyone saw the bright light. Lily smiled. The dark office was no longer scary.

The whole room looked happy and warm. The sun picture made everyone feel good. When the children left, they promised to feed the printer and give it water. That way the printer would always print nice pictures for the class.

A new office printer woke up one morning. It printed the very first page ever it would print. The first page was a box with words on it. "Hello," the box said. After many days, the printer printed again. This time it printed a map with a little path leading to a cookie jar. The dog would have liked that. The people cheered. The printer hummed and beeped happily.

An old office printer was very slow. Every time someone asked it to print, it took forever. First the printer printed one page. Then it printed one more page. Then one more. It was like printing takes a very long time. A little bee landed near the printer. The bee was curious. She listened to the slow clicks and whirs. "Why is this so slow?" she asked the bee. Another bee came closer. "Maybe we should help," she said. So the bees stood on the paper tray. They pushed gently so the printer could move faster. Then the printer printed the whole book quickly. Everyone was happy. Bees and printers worked together. The lesson was: help others when they are slow, and things go faster.

The flower taught a lesson: if something falls, do not run away. Just stop and stay safe.

Leo looked up and could not find the map. He felt sad. Then he saw the map at the top of the tree. It had a tear in it from flying in the wind. Leo climbed the ladder and got the map safely. Now Leo knew where to look for treasure. He smiled and printed another map.

It helped push the paper through. And guess what? The printer worked again! A new page came out. It was a picture of Ruby with her friends. Ruby cried happy tears. She learned that a kind helper can fix almost anything. Even a spoon can be brave when someone needs it.

She saw her own face drawn there. She waddled over and looked at herself. Then she quacked with joy. "That is my picture!" she said. The boy smiled. Dot was not lonely anymore. The lesson is: write thank-you notes so everyone feels loved.

One day Daisy was late and the printer had no paper. The printer felt sad and quiet. Daisy heard the printer and felt bad. Daisy started to cry. A colorful bird came and brought a stack of paper. The colorful bird said I will help you. Together they gave paper to the printer. The printer printed a nice card. Daisy learned that when you are sad you can call a friend for help. Even animals can be helpful when someone needs them.

She looked at the papers and realized the letters were all mixed up. She typed the invitations again. This time, they were right side up. Grandpa came to the party with a big smile. Everyone clapped. Grandpa said, "Thank you, Ivy." The printer did not mind. It just did its job. Ivy learned that careful work makes things better for everyone who comes to enjoy them.

She said, "What a pretty picture, Max." Max smiled and hugged his paper friend. He learned that adding color makes printed pictures come alive.

It grew into a bright orange flower. Pam learned that even small seeds can grow into wonderful things.

A friendly helper came. The helper saw the toy car on the printer. The helper helped the printer lift the toy car. Then the printer unjammed and printed a drawing of the toy car. The boy smiled and took the drawing. The printer was happy again. The toy car stayed on the table where the boy left it. The helper walked away. The printer hummed quietly and waited for the next time someone needed help.

The loud printer was dry and tired of counting. It decided to make a drum sound to have fun. The quiet printer tried to fit close to the rabbit but the drum sound was too loud. The rabbit hid behind a chair. The quiet printer was also sad now. Then both printers sat together without making any noise. The rabbit came out and sniffed them. The rabbit said thank you. The two printers were friends again, soft and quiet.

The printer took a paper and started to work. But something happened. A note fell from the paper tray. The note landed on the floor and blew away in the wind. The printer could not find the note. Leo called out for the note. "Take it, please!" he said. A teacher heard and came quickly. She found the note under a desk. She handed it back to the printer. The printer printed Leo's drawing of a fish. The fish was red and shiny. The whole class clapped for the red fish picture the next day.

Out came a picture of the car, all drawn in blue. The boy looked at the picture and laughed. Now he could play with his car in the picture, even though the real car was stuck under the bed. The printer fixed itself while the boy helped. They were both happy again.

"I am too small to fly up there," said Dot. An apple sat on the table beside the printer. "Do not be scared," said the apple. "I once fell too. But I landed safely." Dot felt braver. He climbed onto a piece of paper and slid down to the floor. He found another drop and they held hands. Together they went up through the slot in the table. They reached the moon! Dot saw the silver light. He felt amazed. Then the wind came and pushed them back. They slid safely down to the apple. Dot was full of wonder. He promised to tell the printer everything he saw. The apple smiled. Dot knew that even small things can have big adventures if they are brave.

Once upon a time, Ruby had a printer. The printer was on the desk. It hummed and beeped. One day, Ruby put a sparkly sheet into the tray. A tiny drop of ink fell out. "Oh," said the drop. "I want to go see the world." The drop rolled down the page. It got very small. "I will wait for you," said Ruby. "I will stay right here." The drop beeped softly and sat still. Soon, another drop fell near it. "Hello," said the second drop. "Where are you going?" "I am going to see the sky!" said the first drop. They rolled together down the page. They went outside in the warm sunshine. The drops saw a red car go by. They saw the blue sky above. They beeped a happy song. "We did it," said the first drop. Ruby smiled at her two tiny drops. She did not need to go far. Her printer had already shown her all there was to see.

The printer felt brave. Ivy turned on the flashlight. The printer started to print. The pages came out slowly. The paper was warm and light. The printer made a picture of the house for Ivy. The picture showed the house lit up. Ivy looked at the picture and smiled. She put the picture on the wall. The picture made the room bright again. The printer learned that being scared is okay, but you can ask for help. Ivy brought light and the printer felt safe. From then on, Ivy always stayed close when the printer worked at night.

Once upon a time there was a blank sheet of paper. It sat on a table and felt very funny. It wanted to become a picture of something fun. "I wish I could play," the paper said softly. A little printer hummed close by. "I can help you," the printer said. So the printer took the paper and printed a big red circle on it. Then it added yellow lines inside the circle. The paper smiled. "That is so much fun!" The paper was happy now. It had learned that even a blank thing can become something good if someone helps it.

A little fish wanted to see what his picture would look like. His mother asked a printer to print a menu for their pretend restaurant. The printer took a piece of paper. "Please print it neat," the mother said. The printer hummed and beeped. It printed the menu in just a few seconds. The paper came out very neat and tidy. There were words for food on one side and a drawing of a fish on the other side. The fish looked at his menu and smiled. "This looks wonderful!" Everyone in the restaurant was happy.

A little bird sat on a chair and wanted to see its picture come out of the printer. "Can you print me?" the bird asked the printer. The printer hummed quietly. It took a special paper and started to print. Slowly, the bird appeared on the page! It had wings and a long neck. The bird chirped with joy. "Thank you!" it said. The little boy who owned the printer clapped his hands. He printed many more pictures of birds after that. The bird felt so glad to be seen.

Tom sat at a table with a printer. He wanted to print silly jokes for his friend Amy. "Let's print some jokes," Tom said. The printer started to print. "Why did the pillow go to the party? Because it wanted to be a cushion!" Tom read the joke out loud. "Ha ha!" said Tom. Amy laughed. "That is funny," she said. Tom kept printing more jokes. One joke made Amy giggle. Another joke made her roll on the floor. They both laughed until their tummies hurt. Printing jokes was the best fun Tom had ever had.

A rabbit was sitting near the printer. "Please stop printing," the rabbit said. But the printer kept printing and printing and printing. Pages piled up on the table. The rabbit felt sleepy. "I am too sleepy to play," the rabbit mumbled. Tom came running over. "What is happening?" he asked. "The printer will not stop," the rabbit said. Tom turned the printer off. The printer stopped. Then Tom cleaned the paper tray. "Good job, Tom," said the rabbit. Tom smiled. The rabbit curled up under a blanket and fell fast asleep.

Once there was a soccer ball on a table. It was sad because the printer next to it would not work right. The printer was slow and grumpy. "I cannot wait to play," the soccer ball sighed. A friendly repair worker came with small tools. He looked at the printer. Then he found a tiny bolt that was loose. He tightened it. The printer hummed again. "You are glad now," the repair worker said. The soccer ball bounced happily. Later, the soccer ball was printed as a picture and hung on the wall. It still lived on the table and played with its friends every day.

Kate wanted to print a picture of her whole family. She fed a big stack of paper into the printer. The printer hummed and began to print. Just as the last page came out, a car drove past the window. The wind pushed the air and the paper lifted up from the table. The paper flew out of the window. Kate looked out the glass. The paper floated away into the sky. She watched until it disappeared. Her family felt sad for a moment. Then Kate had an idea. She printed another bigger picture to go with the first one. Now the whole family was together on one big page again.

Tom walked into the library and found a printer. A book with a flower on its cover was resting on the printer's tray. "I want to print this book," Tom said. The printer hummed and began to print. But then water splashed onto the paper. The ink ran away. The flower on the page looked messy. Tom tried to save the paper. But the book was ruined. Tom felt upset. "Oh no," he said. The librarian saw the wet paper and helped dry it. Later, Tom printed the book again. The flower looked beautiful once more. Tom was happy the second time.

Amy found a tiny robot inside a basket in the back of a shop. The robot fixed broken printers. "Hello, I am Amy," she said. "You are calm and helpful," the robot replied. Amy put the robot to work on a broken printer. The robot found a missing wire and plugged it in. The printer hummed again. "Thank you," Amy said to the robot. The robot beeped happily. Soon a nice customer came to buy the printer. Amy sold the printer and gave the robot a cookie. The robot ate the cookie and went home smiling. Amy kept the robot in the basket to help more printers in the future.

Once there was a printer on a table. When it printed, it hummed a soft pink song. Kate sat beside it and watched. "I want to visit your song," Kate said gently. The printer beeped. "I will hum it for you," the printer said. Kate closed her eyes and listened. The pink notes floated around the room. Later that week, Kate's sister got sick and lay in bed feeling blue. Kate sat next to her sister. "Close your eyes," Kate said. "I will visit you with my song." The pink music filled the room. After a while, the sister felt better and smiled. Kate visited her sister every day with the printer's song.

Bo sat at a table with a printer. He wanted to print a drawing of a tree. But when he pressed the button, nothing happened. The printer made a sad sound. "What is wrong?" Bo asked. The printer said, "I do not have any toner." Bo looked into the printer. There was no dark stuff left to print with. The paper sat there waiting. Bo thought for a moment. Then he got a pencil from his pocket. He drew a tree directly on the blank paper. He did not use the printer at all. He held the paper up and showed it to everyone. "This is my tree," Bo said proudly. He learned that sometimes a person can make something good without any printer.

Once upon a time, a girl was sitting near an open window. She had a printed page in her hands. She was about to print a drawing of a butterfly. The wind blew and the page flew out of her hands. It flew up and out the window and landed on a flower. The flower looked at the paper and thought it was a friend. The paper had paint on it from the sky. The flower whispered, "I will keep you safe under my leaves now." The girl watched from inside and waved goodbye to her paper friend. The butterfly on the paper could not fly away that day.

Once upon a time, Max had a printed page. Max wanted to make a boat from the paper. He folded it and folded it again. But the paper was too small. His sister Amy came into the room. "Max, why are you making a boat?" she asked. "Because I want to float it in the water," said Max. Amy laughed and said, "A tiny boat will sink fast." Max did not listen. He put the boat in a small tub of water. The boat sank right away. Max felt sad. Amy took another printed page and helped him make a bigger boat. Now they both had boats on the water. Max felt proud of his new boat.

Once upon a time, it was Monday at school. The children wished for nice weather today. Their teacher had a printer in the classroom. The teacher printed pictures of clouds. Each child got a cloud picture to color. Little Tim colored his cloud blue. Sally colored hers white. Everyone loved their cloud pictures. The teacher said, "These clouds look like real clouds outside." The children learned that wishes can come true when you print them. A simple lesson is: you do not need to wish very hard. Just ask nicely and the machine does the rest.

Once upon a time, Tess was playing with her little brother in the yard. Her mom had to print a recipe for dinner. The printer hummed and hummed but it would not work. Tess said, "I can help my brother fix it." She went inside and turned the printer off and on again. Beep. Beep. The light blinked. Now it worked! Tess said, "Thank you, brother!" The printer rested and was ready again. A simple lesson is: when you feel tired, stop and rest. Your body needs rest too.

Once upon a time, Kim wanted to print a birthday card. Kim pressed the button and the printer said, "Wait." Then it blinked once. Kim said, "Are you okay?" The printer did not answer. Kim pressed again. The light blinked twice. "I think something is wrong," Kim said softly. She looked at the round screen. The screen showed a party hat with no decorations. Kim took a marker and drew stars on the hat. Now it was a pretty party hat. The printer beeped and printed the card. Kim was happy. A small hint was when the printer only printed one thing. Later, Kim figured it out by adding a decoration on her own.

Once upon a time, a rabbit saw a robot carrying a stack of paper. "Can you help me?" the rabbit called. The robot said, "Yes, I will bring the paper to your friend the printer." The robot carried the paper to the printer. The printer was very loud and wild. The printer rolled back and forth printing a long song on the paper. The rabbit waited quietly by the door. When the paper was done, the robot handed it to the rabbit. "Thank you, friend," said the rabbit. A lesson is: even quiet helpers can do big jobs. You do not have to run fast to be useful.

Once upon a time, an old printer sat on the table in the kitchen. The cat walked over to it and meowed. The printer did not answer. The cat sat on top of the printer. Then rain came down outside. The cat opened one eye at the printer. "I will visit you," said the cat softly. The printer tried to print but it was very slow. One dot appeared. Then another. The cat waited patiently. Finally the printer printed one whole line. The cat purred. The old printer was slow, but it still worked. A lesson is: being slow does not mean you are broken. Good things take time.
